newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Kansas dealers take protection.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Kansas dealers take protection.

text.p: Grain dealers in Kansas were taking scattered two to three cents protection on hard red winter wheat Friday morning after CBOT wheat trended lower in overnight Project A dealings.
KCBT HRW wheat futures were being called lower on signals the market was technically overbought.
Traders said wheat was also likely to follow corn and soybeans, which were subject to lower calls amid forecasts for cooler, damper weather in the Corn Belt early next week.
Meanwhile, basis bids for hard red winter wheat were mostly unchanged, although bids at the Gulf firmed slightly.
Farmer sales of HRW wheat remained active as a result of a net higher wheat market this week, dealers said.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
